content.text:
Fix a data-isolation bug in the Lift Detail view: viewing any lift shows the
same schedules/inspections/defects/rectifications as every other lift,
because the backend ignores the lift filter the frontend already sends.

Confirmed root causes:

1. `backend/src/controllers/scheduling/schedulingController.js` — `listSchedules`
   only reads `{ status, date }` from req.query and never applies a `liftId`
   filter, so `Schedule.find(filter)` returns every schedule.

2. `backend/src/controllers/inspections/inspectionController.js` —
   `listInspections` only reads `{ status, q }`, same missing `liftId` filter.

3. `backend/src/controllers/defects/defectController.js` — `listDefects`
   only reads `{ status, severity, q }`, same missing `liftId` filter.

4. `backend/src/controllers/rectifications/rectificationController.js` —
   `listRectifications` reads no query params at all and always does
   `Rectification.find({ isDeleted: false })`. Rectification has no direct
   `liftId` field — it only links via `defectId` — so filtering by lift here
   requires joining through the referenced Defect's `liftId`.

5. Param name mismatch: the frontend (`LiftDetailDialog.jsx`) calls each
   fetch with `{ lift: lift._id }`, but the Schedule/Defect/Inspection
   models use the field name `liftId`. Standardize on `liftId` as the query
   param name across frontend and backend so this doesn't silently
   no-op again.

6. `schedulingController.js` — `createSchedule` destructures req.body as
   `{ townCouncil, liftCompany, blockAddress, scheduledDate, assignedInspector,
   notes }` and never reads or stores `liftId`, even though
   `ScheduleFormDialog.jsx` collects and submits it via `LiftSelect`. Fix
   `createSchedule` to also destructure and persist `liftId`. Note:
   `updateSchedule` already spreads req.body wholesale so it does persist
   liftId on edits — only `createSchedule` needs the fix.

Required changes:

- Add `liftId` filtering to `listSchedules`, `listInspections`, and
  `listDefects` (filter by `req.query.liftId` when present).
- Add `liftId` filtering to `listRectifications` by resolving matching
  Defect IDs for the given lift first (e.g. `Defect.find({ liftId }).distinct('_id')`)
  and filtering Rectification by `defectId: { $in: ... }`.
- Fix `createSchedule` to accept and store `liftId` from req.body.
- Rename the frontend's fetch param from `lift` to `liftId` in
  `LiftDetailDialog.jsx` (and anywhere else calling these four fetch
  functions with the old `lift` key), so it matches the backend filter.
- Flag as a known data gap (do NOT silently auto-fix without confirming):
  any Schedule documents created before this fix will have `liftId: null`
  and won't retroactively associate with a lift — note this in the PR/commit
  description so the team can decide whether a backfill migration is needed.
- Add/update tests covering: fetching schedules/inspections/defects/
  rectifications scoped to a specific lift returns only that lift's records,
  and that other lifts' records are excluded.

Do not change unrelated behavior (existing status/date/severity/q filters
must keep working alongside the new liftId filter)

All clear. Here's a summary of the fix.

## Summary

**Root cause confirmed and fixed:** the backend list endpoints for schedules, inspections, and defects silently ignored a `liftId` query param the frontend never actually sent (it sent `lift` instead — a naming mismatch on top of the missing filter), and rectifications had no lift-scoping at all despite only linking to a lift indirectly through its defect.

**Backend changes:**
- [schedulingController.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/src/controllers/scheduling/schedulingController.js) — `listSchedules` now filters on `req.query.liftId` alongside the existing `status`/`date` filters. `createSchedule` now destructures and persists `liftId` from the request body (it was silently dropped before).
- [inspectionController.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/src/controllers/inspections/inspectionController.js) — `listInspections` now filters on `liftId` alongside `status`/`q`.
- [defectController.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/src/controllers/defects/defectController.js) — `listDefects` now filters on `liftId` alongside `status`/`severity`/`q`.
- [rectificationController.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/src/controllers/rectifications/rectificationController.js) — `listRectifications` resolves the target lift's Defect IDs first (`Defect.find({ liftId }).distinct('_id')`) and filters `Rectification` by `defectId: { $in: ... }`, since Rectification has no direct lift field.

**Frontend change:**
- [LiftDetailDialog.jsx](em-services-lift-servicing/frontend/src/features/lifts/LiftDetailDialog.jsx) — all four fetch calls now send `{ liftId: lift._id }` instead of `{ lift: lift._id }`, matching the backend's param name. No other callers used the old `lift` key.

**Tests added** (all passing): lift-scoped filtering for schedules ([Aeric](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/tests/Aeric/placeholder.test.js)), defects ([Elijah](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/tests/Elijah/placeholder.test.js)), inspections ([Javier](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/tests/Javier/placeholder.test.js)), and rectifications-via-defect-join ([Ryan](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/tests/Ryan/rectification.test.js)) — each verifies one lift's records come back and another lift's are excluded. Also added a test confirming `createSchedule` now persists `liftId`.

**Pre-existing, unrelated issue found while testing:** `tests/Aeric/placeholder.test.js` had 6 failing tests *before* any of my changes — they assert `res.body._id`/`res.body.status` directly, but the controller wraps all responses in `{ success, message, data }`. I left these alone per the "don't change unrelated behavior" instruction; my two new tests in that file pass correctly using the real envelope shape.

**Known data gap — flagging, not auto-fixing:** any `Schedule` documents created before this fix have `liftId: null` and won't retroactively associate with a lift. The team should decide whether a backfill migration (e.g. matching on `blockAddress`) is worth writing, or whether historical schedules are simply expected to show up as "no lift link."

Expand the search filters on the Lift Workflow search screen
(frontend/src/features/lift-workflow/LiftSearchScreen.jsx) and make the
categorical filters multi-select.

Current state:
- Only 3 filters exist: free-text `search` (matches liftCode/block/unit),
  `statusFilter` (single-select dropdown), `typeFilter` (single-select
  dropdown).
- Filtering happens client-side in a `useMemo` over the full `lifts` array
  already fetched via `liftApi.fetchLifts()`.
- Lift fields available (see backend/src/models/lifts/Lift.js) but not yet
  filterable: `manufacturer`, `capacity`, `installDate`, `lastServiced`.
- `LIFT_TYPES` and `LIFT_STATUSES` enums come from
  frontend/src/utils/liftHelpers.js.

Required changes:

1. Convert `statusFilter` and `typeFilter` from single-select `TextField
   select` to multi-select controls (MUI `Select multiple` with checkboxes,
   or `Autocomplete multiple` — match whatever multi-select pattern, if any,
   is already used elsewhere in the app for consistency). Each should default
   to "all" (empty selection = no filtering on that field) and show selected
   chips/summary text.

2. Add a **manufacturer** filter — multi-select, options derived dynamically
   from the distinct `manufacturer` values present in the loaded `lifts`
   array (don't hardcode a list, since manufacturers aren't a fixed enum).

3. Add a **block** filter — multi-select, options derived dynamically from
   distinct `block` values in the loaded lifts (same reasoning as
   manufacturer).

4. Add a **capacity range** filter (min/max numeric inputs, or a slider) to
   filter lifts by `capacity`.

5. Add a **last serviced date range** filter (from/to date pickers) filtering

6. Update the `filteredLifts` useMemo to apply all new filters using

7. Add a "Clear filters" button that resets all filter state at once.

8. Keep this screen read-only (no create/edit/delete) and keep the single-row

9. Keep filtering client-side (consistent with the current implementation)

## Summary

Added a compact, two-part status summary to the Lift Workflow header ([LiftWorkflowPage.jsx](em-services-lift-servicing/frontend/src/features/lift-workflow/LiftWorkflowPage.jsx)), next to the existing `liftCode`/block/unit/status chip:

**1. Stage chip** (outlined, so it reads as secondary to the lift's own status chip) — answers "where is this lift in the Schedule → Inspection → Defect → Rectification chain right now," picked furthest-along-first so it always reflects the most operationally relevant thing:
open defect(s) → awaiting rectification endorsement / rectification in draft → inspection in progress → spot-check pending → not yet scheduled → up to date.

**2. Warning icon + tooltip** (only rendered when something's actually stuck) — answers "is anything overdue," listing every applicable reason:
- a spot-check past its scheduled date that's still open (reused the existing `isOverdue` helper from `scheduleHelpers.js`)
- a defect open past a severity-scaled grace period (Critical 3d / Major 7d / Minor 14d — a defect isn't automatically "stuck" the instant it's logged)
- a rectification `Submitted` 7+ days ago with no endorsement yet

New file [useLiftWorkflowStatus.js](em-services-lift-servicing/frontend/src/features/lift-workflow/useLiftWorkflowStatus.js) fetches this one lift's slice of all four modules via the `?liftId=` server-side filters (added in an earlier fix) and reduces them to those two indicators; it re-fetches whenever `activeStep` changes so stepping through the wizard picks up anything just created in the previous step.

**Scoped out on purpose, per the brief:** no metrics panel, no repeat of the lift's own status chip, no indicator added "because the data exists" (e.g. didn't add a raw open-defect-count badge separate from the stage chip, since the stage chip already leads with that when it's the most relevant fact). Also skipped the "compact column on `LiftSearchScreen`" option — computing this per-row would mean fetching 4 collections per lift in the list (N+1), which conflicts with "keep it high-signal, not a dashboard" and the list's existing pure-client-side-filter design; flagging that as a deliberate scope decision rather than an oversight.

**Verification:** added `frontend/tests/LiftWorkflow/useLiftWorkflowStatus.test.js` (19 tests, all passing via new `npm run test:workflow`) covering the stage-priority logic and each attention-reason threshold; `npm run build` is clean.

Fix: endorsing a Rectification doesn't update the linked Defect's status.

Root cause: endorseRectification in
backend/src/controllers/rectifications/rectificationController.js:155-175
only mutates the Rectification document itself (status -> 'Endorsed',
endorsedBy, endorsedDate). It never touches the Defect referenced by
`existing.defectId`, so after endorsement the defect is left at whatever
status it already had (e.g. still "Open" or "In Progress") even though the
whole point of endorsement is that LMS staff have confirmed, after a joint
on-site inspection, that the defect is actually fixed.

Required fix:
- In endorseRectification, after setting the rectification to 'Endorsed',
  also advance the linked Defect's status forward, using the SAME
  transition rules already enforced in
  backend/src/controllers/defects/defectController.js (VALID_TRANSITIONS):
    Open: ['In Progress', 'Closed']
    'In Progress': ['Resolved', 'Open']
    Resolved: ['Closed', 'In Progress']
    Closed: ['Open']
  Don't hardcode a single target status (e.g. always set 'Closed') without
  checking the defect's current status against this map first - a defect
  currently 'In Progress' can only move to 'Resolved' or 'Open' per the
  existing rules, not directly to 'Closed'. Decide the correct target
  status for each current state (most likely: 'Open' -> 'Closed',
  'In Progress' -> 'Resolved', already 'Resolved'/'Closed' -> no-op) and
  apply it consistently with how defectController.js's updateDefect already
  transitions status (including setting `resolvedDate` the same way
  updateDefect does when a defect first reaches 'Resolved').
- Do this by importing the Defect model into rectificationController.js
  (it's already imported for assertDefectExists) and updating the
  referenced defect in the same handler, in the same request/transaction as
  the rectification's own save - don't leave it as a separate manual step.
- Consider whether VALID_TRANSITIONS should be exported from
  defectController.js (it already is, per its module.exports) and imported
  here, rather than re-declaring the same map a second time - reuse it
  instead of duplicating it.
- If the defect is already 'Closed' or in some other state where the
  target transition isn't valid per the map, decide whether to silently
  skip updating it (defect already resolved by other means) or surface a
  warning - don't throw and block the endorsement itself, since the
  rectification endorsement is the primary action here and shouldn't fail
  because of a downstream defect-status edge case.
- Add a test covering: endorsing a rectification whose defect is
  'In Progress' moves the defect to 'Resolved' (with resolvedDate set);
  endorsing one whose defect is already 'Open' moves it to 'Closed'.

Do not change any other endorsement behavior (the Submitted-only gate,
endorsedBy requirement, locking photos/signature) - this is additive.

content.text:
Confirmed: `nextDefectNo()` (and the equivalent `nextReportNo()` for inspections) scan `Defect.find({})`/`Inspection.find({})` with no `isDeleted` filter. Since `deleteDefect`/`deleteInspection` were switched from hard deletes to soft deletes at some point in this codebase's history, a "deleted" record still counts toward the "current max number" scan, so the number-reuse-after-delete tests now fail. This predates my change and is unrelated to rectification endorsement — out of scope here, but worth flagging separately since it's a real bug (defect/report numbers will now permanently skip ahead instead of reusing freed numbers, contrary to the documented intent in both controllers' comments).

## Summary

Fixed [rectificationController.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/src/controllers/rectifications/rectificationController.js):

- **Imported `VALID_TRANSITIONS`** from `defectController.js` instead of re-declaring it — single source of truth.
- **Added `ENDORSEMENT_TARGET_STATUS`** (`Open → Closed`, `In Progress → Resolved`) describing where endorsement should push a defect from each starting status. `Resolved`/`Closed` have no entry, so they're left alone.
- **`endorseRectification`** now, after saving the rectification as `Endorsed`, looks up the linked `Defect`, checks `ENDORSEMENT_TARGET_STATUS[defect.status]` against `VALID_TRANSITIONS[defect.status]` (so it can never attempt a jump the model itself would reject), applies the transition, and — mirroring `updateDefect` exactly — sets `resolvedDate` the first time a defect reaches `Resolved`. All in the same handler/request, no separate step.
- If the defect is missing, already soft-deleted, or already at `Resolved`/`Closed` (no valid forward jump), it's silently skipped — the rectification's own endorsement still succeeds and is never blocked by a downstream defect-status edge case.
- Left the Submitted-only gate, `endorsedBy` requirement, and photo/signature locking untouched.

**Tests added** to [tests/Ryan/rectification.test.js](em-services-lift-servicing/backend/tests/Ryan/rectification.test.js) (all 30 tests in the suite pass):
- endorsing a rectification whose defect is `In Progress` → defect becomes `Resolved` with `resolvedDate` set
- endorsing one whose defect is `Open` → defect becomes `Closed` directly (not routed through `Resolved`)
- endorsing one whose defect is already `Closed` → endorsement still succeeds (200), defect stays `Closed` (confirms the "never throw" requirement)

Verified no circular-require issue from the new cross-controller import, and re-ran the full backend suite — no new failures introduced by this change.
